name: Conversion of Boris I
summary: Boris I, Khan of Bulgaria, is baptized as a Christian (864) under Byzantine pressure following a military defeat. He initially sought a Bulgarian patriarchate from Rome (866) but ultimately aligned with Constantinople when the Eastern Church offered more favorable terms. His son Simeon I's Cyrillic literacy program, building on Cyril and Methodius's work, makes Bulgaria the center of Slavic Christian culture. Boris abdicates (889) to become a monk, later returning to depose his pagan son Vladimir.

_quarry.structural_significance: Aligns Bulgaria with Byzantine Orthodox Christianity; enables Slavic literacy through the Cyrillic alphabet; transforms Bulgaria from a pagan khanate to a Christian kingdom with imperial pretensions
